title: Sessions at Jimmy Yancey's house, Cripple Clarence Lofton, Preston Jackson
summary: Lovett recalls sessions at Yancey's house where Lofton played, and says he played with Preston Jackson and Baby Dodds only at the concert.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, we'll try to find them. We talked about the styles that you were emulating. It seems to me that the trombone might also.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah, well, I'd say he was probably vaguely influenced by King Ori and Jim Robinson. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. But I don't think he was... I don't think he listened to jazz that closely. I mean, I don't...
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, now that I think of it, you might also say it may be Jimmy Archie, because it's a puffing kind of performance that might even be more Archie than Ori.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I remember we played some sessions at Jimmy Yancey's house. And people like Cripple Clarence Lofton would come in. I remember that. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And you played with him? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. With Jimmy. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. You remember ever playing with Lofton? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I don't think I ever actually played with him, but I was there one night when he came in and sat down and played.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Just lately I've written a note about Lofton saying that because it was difficult for people to play with him, not many say that they sat in with Lofton. Even drummers found it a little difficult. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Since he was a soloist and so much an individualist. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. But no problem playing with Jimmy Yancey, of course. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No, no.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Played the standard blues. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, he liked us very much, I remember.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. You don't remember recording with Jimmy Yancey? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No, I don't think we did. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Were there other New Orleans people you know? Now you mentioned at the concert, Preston Jackson, did you ever work with him again? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No, I think that was the only time I ever saw him or played with him. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And Baby Dodds, do you remember working with him elsewhere?
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I don't actually remember working with him anywhere else.
